reading.h2: St. Cyril of Alexandria: The Seal of the Fathers

reading.p: This lesson introduces St. Cyril of Alexandria (Abba Kirillos), his defense of the one incarnate Christ against the Nestorian error, and why his teaching is the foundation of the Ethiopian Tewahedo faith.

list: 24th Pope and Patriarch of Alexandria (412–444 AD)
Nephew of Theophilus of Alexandria, a powerful defender of the Orthodox faith
Raised and trained within Church leadership

reading.p: Alexandria is the Mother Church of Ethiopia, and our faith flows through St. Cyril’s teachings.
He is called “The Seal of the Fathers” because he preserved and completed the teachings of those before him.

The great question is this: Is Jesus Christ one person or two? Is He God, man, or both? The Tewahedo answer is that He is one united nature (Tewahedo) and one person — the incarnate Word of God, fully God and fully Man.
Why it matters: if Christ is divided, His suffering cannot save us. To know Christ correctly is to know God correctly.

reading.h2: The Core Issue: Who Is Christ?

reading.p: The great question of the early Church was how Christ’s divinity and humanity are united. Is He divided? Is He one? How can God truly become man? This question led to a major theological conflict known as the Nestorian Controversy — the Christological controversy of the fifth century, the debate over the nature of Christ.

Nestorius was the Bishop of Constantinople — one of the highest Church positions — an influential preacher and teacher whose teachings spread quickly across the empire. In his approach, he relied heavily on human reasoning and struggled to accept the mystery of God becoming man.
He was situated among the five ancient Church Sees, the Pentarchy: Rome, Constantinople, Alexandria, Antioch, and Jerusalem.

Nestorius taught what may be called the “two-person” error: that Christ is two separate persons — one human (Jesus) and one divine (the Son of God) — and that God only “dwelt in” the man Jesus, like a person living in a house. The key problem is that this creates two Sons instead of one Christ.

Nestorius rejected the title Theotokos (Mother of God), claiming that Mary gave birth only to the human Jesus. The danger is clear: if Mary is not the Mother of God, then the one born is not truly God. This divides Christ.

reading.h2: The Problem with a Divided Christ

reading.p: Nestorius was condemned because a “mere man” cannot save the world and a “mere man” cannot forgive sins. If God did not truly suffer for us, then we are not truly saved. The Tewahedo truth is that God the Word suffered in the flesh for us.

St. Cyril taught the miracle of the union (Tewahedo): Christ is ONE, not two — fully God and fully man. In the Incarnation, the Word did not merely visit a man; the Word became man. He is one unified Christ.

reading.h2: The Analogy of Iron and Fire

reading.p: To understand Tewahedo, consider iron placed in fire, which becomes red-hot. In their unity, the iron and the fire are united and act as one. Yet there is no confusion: fire does not become iron, and iron does not become fire. And there is no separation: you cannot strike the iron without touching the heat. This is Christ — one united reality out of two.

Mary is called the Gate of Light. Since Christ is God, and Mary gave birth to Christ, therefore Mary is the Mother of God (Theotokos). The key truth is that honoring Mary protects the truth about Christ.
The contrast between the error of Nestorius and the Tewahedo faith of St. Cyril is sharp.

list: Nestorius: two persons. St. Cyril: One Person.
Nestorius: separation. St. Cyril: perfect unity.
Nestorius: Mary is the mother of a man. St. Cyril: Mary is the Mother of God.
Nestorius: salvation weakened. St. Cyril: salvation complete.

reading.p: At the Council of Ephesus, the victory of truth, 200 bishops gathered, led by St. Cyril of Alexandria. As a result, Nestorius was rejected, the Theotokos was affirmed, and Christ was declared ONE.

reading.h2: Did This Cause a Church Split?

reading.p: At Ephesus (431 AD), Nestorius was rejected and the Church remained united. The split happened later, at Chalcedon (451 AD).
The agreement among all was that Christ is fully God and fully man. The difference was over how to describe Christ’s union, expressed in two ways:

list: Tewahedo: one united nature.
Chalcedon: two natures united.

reading.p: The faith of the Church is one Lord Jesus Christ, perfect in His divinity and perfect in His humanity. Importantly, we do not speak of Christ as divided after the union. He is ONE.
This is the Mia Physis formula: “One incarnate nature of God the Word.” The union works in this way:

list: No mixing
No confusion
No alteration
No division

reading.p: It is perfect unity.

Our Church is called Tewahedo because of this belief in the unity of Christ. Our Liturgy (the Kidassie) teaches the unity of Christ, and in the Eucharist we receive the true Body and Blood of the one united Christ.

St. Cyril matters because his teaching protects our faith. Many today say Jesus was just a prophet or teacher, but if Jesus is not God, we have no salvation. The lesson is that truth is worth defending.

list: Christ is ONE, not two.
Divinity and humanity are united.
The Theotokos protects Christ’s identity.
Tewahedo means unity.
How does knowing Christ is both God and man change your faith?
Why is “Tewahedo” important to our identity?
How can you defend your faith today?

reading.quote: He made His humanity one with His divinity, without mixture, without confusion, without change, without division.

reading.p: Glory be to the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. Amen.

studyGuide.overview: This lesson presents St. Cyril of Alexandria, the ‘Seal of the Fathers,’ and his defense of the one incarnate Christ against the error of Nestorius, who divided Christ into two persons and rejected the title Theotokos. It explains the Tewahedo (Miaphysite) confession of one united nature of God the Word — fully God and fully man, united without mixing, confusion, alteration, or division — and why this faith, affirmed at Ephesus in 431 AD, defines the Ethiopian Tewahedo identity.
keyPoints: St. Cyril was the 24th Pope and Patriarch of Alexandria (412–444 AD), called the ‘Seal of the Fathers.’
Nestorius’ error divided Christ into two persons and denied Mary the title Theotokos, which divides Christ.
A divided or ‘mere man’ Christ cannot save or forgive; God the Word truly suffered in the flesh for us.
St. Cyril taught that the Word became man, forming one unified Christ — the formula ‘One incarnate nature of God the Word.’
The iron-and-fire analogy shows union with no confusion and no separation, while each retains its own reality.
The Council of Ephesus (431 AD) rejected Nestorius and affirmed the Theotokos; the Church remained united, with the split coming later at Chalcedon (451 AD).
The Ethiopian Church is called Tewahedo (‘unity’) because of this belief, taught in the Kidassie and received in the Eucharist.
reviewQuestions: Why is St. Cyril called the ‘Seal of the Fathers’?
What was Nestorius’ ‘two-person’ error, and why is it dangerous?
Why does denying the Theotokos divide Christ?
How does the iron-and-fire analogy explain the union of Christ’s divinity and humanity?
What did the Council of Ephesus decide in 431 AD?
What is the difference between the Tewahedo expression and the Chalcedonian expression of Christ’s union?
How does the doctrine of the one incarnate Christ relate to the Eucharist and to Tewahedo identity?

checks: One incarnate Christ confessed: fully God and fully man, one Person and one united nature (Tewahedo/Miaphysite)
Miaphysite union stated correctly as ‘without mixing, confusion, alteration/change, or division’ — not monophysite absorption
Nestorianism (two persons / two Sons) explicitly rejected
Theotokos affirmed and defended; Council of Ephesus 431 upheld
Chalcedon (451) identified as the later split and its ‘two natures’ formula not adopted
St. Cyril’s ‘One incarnate nature of God the Word’ presented as canonical basis
Eucharist affirmed as the true Body and Blood of the one united Christ
Slide typos repaired without altering doctrine: ‘Fully Go/d’ joined to ‘Fully God,’ and ‘Perfect Unit’ read as ‘perfect unity’
